While type hints indicate Callable type, Python does not enforce these at runtime. Any non-callable object added via append() or other inherited list methods (extend, insert, etc.) will cause a TypeError when send() attempts to invoke it with 'await receiver(*args, **kwargs)'. This is a type confusion vulnerability that can lead to denial of service through unhandled runtime exceptions.

evidence.code_context: Line 58 in aiosignal/__init__.py calls self.append(func) without validation. The Signal class inherits from FrozenList which provides append() method. Line 51 in send() method invokes callbacks with 'await receiver(*args, **kwargs)' assuming they are callable.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: Data flows from __call__ method parameter 'func' -> self.append(func) -> stored in FrozenList -> retrieved in send() method as 'receiver' -> invoked with await receiver(*args, **kwargs). No validation occurs between registration and invocation.
evidence.notes: Type hints exist (Callable[[Unpack[_Ts]], Awaitable[_T]]) but are not enforced at runtime. FrozenList is a third-party library that does not validate item types. Any inherited list method (append, extend, insert, etc.) can bypass the __call__ decorator and add non-callable items.
